content.title: Paradise Season 3 (2027): Renewal, Cast, Final Season
content.text: Key PointsHulu's "Paradise" starring Sterling K. Brown has been renewed for a third and likely final season.Creator Dan Fogelman has previously said he has a "plan for three seasons of the show."The Season 3 renewal came ahead of drama series' Season 2 finale. Thought Hulu was done with Paradise? Think twice. The political thriller, created by Dan Fogelman, has been renewed for a third and final season. “What’s satisfying about this ending in 3 is what’s satisfying about writing a movie, which you get to take someone all the way to the completion of what their arc is,” writer and executive producer John Hoberg exclusively told Parade. Two weeks before the Season 2 finale, Paradise star Sterling K. Brown announced the renewal news in a video, “love actuallying” the camera like Link (played by Thomas Doherty) did earlier in the season. 🎬SIGN UP for Parade’s Daily newsletter to get the latest pop culture news & celebrity interviews delivered right to your inbox 🎬 “Knock knock. Paradise is full of secrets…so many secrets…that they can’t be contained to just 2 seasons,” Brown’s cue cards read, before the words “Paradise will be back for Season 3″ appeared onscreen. The day after the show’s renewal was announcement, Paradise star Enuka Okuma revealed to Parade that creator Dan Fogelman teased her about what’s to come. “He’s just like, ‘You have no clue where it’s going,’” she shared. “And I believe it. I believe it.” Related: ‘Paradise’ Writer Teases ‘Satisfying’ Final Season: ‘We’re Answering Everything’ (Exclusive) Across its first two seasons, the Hulu Original drama series has been streamed globally for nearly 12 billion minutes, with Season 2 amassing over 30 million hours, per Disney. Before the smash hit returns for a third season, here is everything we know so far about Season 3 of Paradise. How to watch Paradise Paradise, a 20th Television production, streams on Hulu and Hulu on Disney+. Related: ‘Paradise’ Star Enuka Okuma on That Long-Awaited Reunion — And Why She Feared It Would End in Tragedy (Exclusive) When is the Paradise Season 3 release date? Hoberg revealed to Parade in March that shooting is set to begin in April 2026. While no premiere date has been announced just yet, but judging by the timing of Season 2, it seems possible that Season 3 could arrive in 2027. The showed first premiered in January 2025 and returned for its second season in February 2026. Related: James Marsden Reveals the Musical Legend He’s ‘Always Wanted’ To Play (Exclusive) Who will be in the Paradise Season 3 cast? The Season 3 cast hasn’t been confirmed, but the series stars Sterling K. Brown, Julianne Nicholson, Sarah Shahi, Nicole Brydon Bloom, Krys Marshall, Enuka Okuma, Aliyah Mastin, Percy Daggs IV and Charlie Evans. James Marsden, Thomas Doherty and Jon Beavers were recurring guest stars in Season 3, along with Shailene Woodley, whose character died in the fourth episode. Paradise stars: Sterling K. Brown as Agent Xavier Collins Enuka Okuma as Dr. Teri Rogers-Collins Julianne Nicholson as Samantha Redmond (codename Sinatra) Krys Marshall as Agent Robinson Nicole Brydon Bloom as Jane Sarah Shahi as Dr. Gabriela Torabi Aliyah Mastin as Presley Collins Percy Daggs IV as James Collins Charlie Evans as the president’s son, Jeremy Related: Sterling K. Brown Finds Power in ‘Difficult Conversations’—They’ve Led Him to Paradise and Beyond (Exclusive) How did Season 2 of Paradise end? The second season ended with the destruction of the bunker. Samantha went down with the mountain, after tasking Xavier with finding the quantum computer Alex, whose identity was revealed in the Season 2 finale. What will happen in Season 3 of Paradise? Season 3 will be “definitive” and “satisfying,” according to Hoberg. Speaking to Parade, the writer revealed: “We’ve left everybody outside of this bunker. Xavier’s been given this mission from Sinatra that he may or may not think is insane and may or may not want to do. And we’re picking up from there with all these sort of unfinished storylines, but a brand new world.” Okuma’s previously told Parade that “anything could happen” next. She said: “Anything could happen, but I’m just excited about how we’ve already expanded the world. The first season was so much confinement in that bunker, and then we discovered that there’s a world out there, and this season, we explored more. And I’m so curious as to how much further we’re going to expand, like ‘Where are we going now?'” Okuma added, “This show, when I talk to Dan about it too, they’re just like, Dan and Sterling both say, ‘Oh, it’s good. Don’t worry it’s good.'” Hoberg confirmed to Parade that in Season 3 fans can expect just as many twists and turns as in previous seasons, along with answers. He said: “We, from the beginning, made a pact, Dan [Fogelman] and I, that this show would not become frustrating because we didn’t answer the big questions. And for two seasons, we’ve done that. We posed a big question and then answered, and so we will not leave people hanging.” Related: ‘Paradise’ Unleashes Its Most Disturbing Twist Yet: Jane’s Chilling Origin Will there be a Season 4 of Paradise? Sadly, no. Fogelman, the creator, has said in the past that he had a “plan for three seasons of the show.” From a storytelling perspective, Hoberg admitted to Parade that he thinks ending the show with Season 3 feels “like the right thing to do.” About the authorAlexandra Hurtado has been writing about entertainment since 2013 and contributing to Parade since 2019. The University of Miami alum has interviewed countless names in the entertainment world, including Morgan Freeman, Elton John, Ben Affleck, Billy Crystal, Eddie Murphy, Tina Fey, Jamie Lee Curtis, Kurt Russell, Pamela Anderson, John Krasinski, Ryan Reynolds and Kate Winslet.
